sections.title: Sec 1: The pH Scale and Logarithms
lecture_lines: pH measures acidity from zero to fourteen.
Red means high hydrogen ion concentration.
Blue means low hydrogen ion concentration.
pH equals negative log base ten.
animations: Animation step 1: A horizontal gradient bar fades in, transitioning from #FF0000 (left) to #0000FF (right). Labels '0' and '14' appear at ends in #FFFFFF.
Animation step 2: A red dot pulses at the left end. Text '[H+] = 1' appears in #FF0000 next to it.
Animation step 3: A blue dot pulses at the right end. Text '[H+] = 1e-14' appears in #0000FF next to it.
Animation step 4: The formula 'pH = -log10[H+]' slides down from the top in #FFFF00. The term '[H+]' highlights in #FF0000.
Animation step 5: A small number '0.0001' shrinks rapidly into a single digit '4' with a compression effect, illustrating the log concept.

sections.title: Sec 2: The Core Formula
lecture_lines: The formula is pH equals negative log.
Concentration is measured in moles per liter.
Logarithms act like a compression tool.
Negative sign flips the result positive.
Higher acidity yields lower pH values.
animations: Animation step 1: A central card appears with 'pH = -log10[H+]' in #FFFFFF. The '[H+]' part glows #FF0000.
Animation step 2: Text 'mol/L' appears below '[H+]' in #00FFFF to indicate units.
Animation step 3: A zipper icon animates over the number '0.001', compressing it into '3' in #FFFF00.
Animation step 4: A minus sign appears before the '3', turning it to '-3', then the outer negative sign cancels it to show '3' in #00FF00.
Animation step 5: An arrow points from high [H+] (left) to low pH number (bottom), emphasizing the inverse relationship.

sections.title: Sec 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
lecture_lines: Given concentration is one times ten power negative three.
Substitute this value into the formula.
Logarithm of ten power negative three is negative three.
Apply the negative sign to the result.
animations: Animation step 1: Text '[H+] = 1 × 10⁻³ M' types out in #FFFFFF on the left side.
Animation step 2: The value '1 × 10⁻³' moves into the formula 'pH = -log10( )' in the center.
Animation step 3: The term 'log10(10⁻³)' highlights, and the result '-3' appears below it in #FF0000.
Animation step 4: The negative sign from the formula combines with '-3', showing '-(-3)' which transforms into '3' in #00FF00.
Animation step 5: The final equation 'pH = 3' glows bright green (#00FF00) and scales up slightly for emphasis.

sections.title: Sec 4: Interpreting the Result
lecture_lines: Place pH three on the scale.
This value indicates an acidic solution.
It is similar to lemon juice.
animations: Animation step 1: The pH scale bar from Section 1 reappears. A marker drops onto the '3' position in #FF0000.
Animation step 2: The area from 0 to 7 highlights in red (#FF0000). Text 'ACIDIC' flashes in #FF0000 above the scale.
Animation step 3: An icon of a lemon appears next to the '3' marker. Text 'Lemon Juice ~ pH 2' appears in #FFFF00.
